answer: No. A 1 second trigger plus a 1 second run gives a p50 near 1.5 s and a p99 near 2.5 s. The median passes the 2 s SLA, but the tail (p99) misses it, and micro-batch fails on the tail. A 2 s SLA tolerates no trigger at all, so the team needs a record-at-a-time engine for the ETA workload, even though it means learning a second runtime. Micro-batch is only a fit for SLAs where the trigger is a fraction of the target.
